scope.note: Phase 3 scope. The synth is a reduced but honest Nord Wave 2-style engine: Analog mode only, an explicit waveform list, four filters, three envelopes, LFO, voice modes, and a deterministic arpeggiator/gate. Items under excluded are never required; their panel controls exist visually but stay decorative and are listed as unsupported.
required: Three layers (A, B, C) with independent state and effect chains
Analog mode with the exact waveform list below and category-correct Osc Ctrl behavior
One FM Harmonic algorithm with Osc Ctrl as FM amount
LP12, LP24, HP, and BP filters with keyboard tracking, resonance, and drive
Oscillator, filter, and amplifier envelopes (attack/decay/release, velocity)
LFO with five waveforms, three destinations, and master-clock sync
Poly/mono/legato voice modes, note priority, glide, unison, vibrato
Arpeggiator/gate with rate, master-clock sync, range, direction, hold, and run
optional: Samples mode with a small bundled sample set
LP M and LP+HP filter types
Sub Osc, Shape, Shape Sine, Misc, and Wave oscillator categories
excluded: Extern mode and everything MIDI-out (manual ch. 8)
Arpeggiator pattern editing, zig-zag, accent, pan, and per-layer KB Hold exclude (manual p. 35-36)
Synth preset library and Nord Sample Library downloads (cut benchmark-wide)

architecture.oledDisplay: The Synth section's OLED shows the selected waveform, envelope curves, and menu values through three dials below it (manual p. 27).

oscCtrlByCategory.Sync: Relative pitch of the synced oscillator (manual p. 29).
oscCtrlByCategory.Multi: Detune amount between the stacked saws (manual p. 30).
oscCtrlByCategory.Super: Detune/width of the oscillator stack (manual p. 30).

oscillator.oscCtrlKnob: 0-10, morphable, modulatable by the oscillator envelope and the LFO (manual p. 28).

envelopes.shared: Attack, decay, and release times set from the display dials; decay at maximum acts as sustain mode (manual p. 33).

lfo.offState: No destination LED lit means the LFO is off but keeps its settings (manual p. 34).

voice.glide: Constant-rate portamento, active in mono/legato when playing legato (manual p. 35).

arpeggiatorGate.rate: Quarter-note BPM, or subdivision (1/2 to 1/16, triplet variants) when synced to the master clock (manual p. 36).
arpeggiatorGate.range: 1-4 octaves (Gate mode repurposes the knob as gate envelope hardness).
arpeggiatorGate.kbHold: Notes keep sounding and the arpeggio keeps running after keys are lifted (manual p. 36).
arpeggiatorGate.run: ARP RUN starts and stops the arpeggiator.
arpeggiatorGate.determinism: With a fixed clock and note set, step order and timing are deterministic and testable.

acceptance: Every required waveform is selectable and Pure, Sync, Multi, Super, and FM-H are audibly distinct source behaviors, with Osc Ctrl acting per category.
Filter type, frequency, resonance, tracking, drive, and envelope amount each alter rendered audio.
All three envelopes and the LFO have observable time-domain or spectral effects, and LFO/arp lock to the master clock.
Mono, legato, priority, glide, unison, and vibrato change voice behavior, not just labels.
Arpeggiator and gate rate, range, direction, hold, and run behave deterministically under a fixed clock.
All three layers integrate with zones, scenes, morphs, programs, and their own effect chains.
